title: Compact collapse + column ghosting: density regulator and resize heuristics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table currently exposes only a single density toggle which causes abrupt reflows, clipped content, and unclear column-resize affordances at compact breakpoints. This ticket defines a "density regulator" system (design tokens + interaction rules) that smoothly transitions between density modes, introduces a "ghosting" state for columns that will collapse, and standardizes resize heuristics so users retain discoverability and control across device sizes and when using keyboard/assistive tech.

Scope: design system tokens for vertical/horizontal spacing, compact typography variants, spec for a column ghosting visual state, interaction rules for predictive collapse (thresholds, reveal delay), keyboard & screen-reader behavior for collapsing columns, and a lightweight Figma prototype + developer handoff with token examples and CSS token names. We will also document perf constraints for virtualization (min frame budget, preferred batch sizes) so eng can implement without regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrating density regulator control and column ghosting states (desktop + narrow breakpoint)
Design tokens added: spacing.small-row / spacing.xs-row, typography.table-compact, token examples and naming conventions committed to design-tokens docs
Interaction spec: resize heuristics doc (drag thresholds, snap-to-fit rules, predictive collapse timeouts) reviewed and signed off by Eng
Accessibility spec: keyboard flows, ARIA announcements, and SR text for collapse/expand published and validated by accessibility reviewer
Developer handoff: component props defined (density, ghostThreshold, collapseDelay) and a reference CSS/JSON token file attached to the PR
Performance guardrails: eng acceptance test shows no more than 5% render-time regression on large table fixtures when enabling ghosting/density regulator
Integration tests: visual snapshots for key density states and a11y automation for keyboard collapse/expand added to table suite
notes:
Key design trade-offs: 1) visual clarity vs. information density — we prefer preserving column headers and hinting collapse rather than immediate removal; 2) token proliferation vs. flexibility — we add a small set of composable tokens scoped to tables instead of many one-off values; 3) virtualization costs — ghosting must be rendered as a lightweight overlay and not force full-cell reflows.

Refer to the investigation doc in Drive for measured density breakpoints we ran with product analytics (links below).
